title: Nvidia partner ChipAgents raises $60M for agentic chip design
excerpt: ChipAgents, a startup building AI agents that design and test semiconductors, has raised $60 million. The company, a partner of Nvidia, is betting that the same agentic AI reshaping software can be turned on the painstaking business of making chips. The raise adds to an already busy year. ChipAgents closed a $21 million Series A […]
content_html:
ChipAgents, a startup building AI agents that design and test semiconductors, has raised $60 million. The company, a partner of Nvidia, is betting that the same agentic AI reshaping software can be turned on the painstaking business of making chips.

The raise adds to an already busy year. ChipAgents closed a $21 million Series A last October and a $50 million round in February, so the latest cheque takes its total funding to roughly $134 million in under a year, a pace that tracks the wider rush into AI-native chip-design tools.

“We’re enabling the industry to move beyond AI assistants toward autonomous agents that can execute meaningful engineering work,” said William Wang, CEO and Founder, ChipAgents.

The company’s product sits in a corner of the industry known as EDA. Electronic design automation is the software engineers use to lay out and verify chips, a market long dominated by a handful of incumbents, and the one ChipAgents wants to rebuild around autonomous agents rather than human-driven tools.

Verification is the bottleneck it is aiming at. Checking that a chip actually does what it is supposed to can eat more than 70% of a design project’s time, and ChipAgents says its agents can read a specification, write the tests, run them, and iterate without an engineer holding their hand at each step.

The claims are bold, as they tend to be. The company says its agents comprehend specifications many times faster than people and generate formal checks almost instantly, and that the platform is already in production at several chipmakers, though those figures come from the company rather than any independent audit.

Its founder frames it as a change of model. William Wang, ChipAgents’ chief executive, describes agents that “read specifications, break down objectives, discuss and implement solutions, validate results and iterate relentlessly,” a pitch for software that does the job rather than assists the person doing it.

The company is the product of Alpha Design AI, based in San Jose with research roots near Santa Barbara. Wang, an academic turned founder, has leaned on that pedigree to recruit both talent and early customers.

The investor base has been heavy on strategics. Earlier rounds drew in Bessemer Venture Partners alongside chip-world names including Micron, MediaTek, and Ericsson, the kind of backers whose interest doubles as a signal that the technology is being taken seriously inside the industry.

The Nvidia label is the eye-catching part. Reuters cast ChipAgents as an Nvidia partner, a useful association in a market where Nvidia’s chips and software sit at the centre of the AI boom, even if the exact terms of the relationship were not spelled out.

It is not alone in the idea. A wave of startups is pitching AI at different layers of the silicon stack, from Oxmiq’s chip architecture to Kandou’s interconnects, and agentic design tools are the newest front in that competition.

The logic is almost recursive. AI needs ever more chips, chips are slow and costly to design, and so the industry is reaching for AI to design the chips that will run more AI, a loop that investors have found hard to resist.

The incumbents are not standing still, which is the risk. The established EDA vendors have their own AI features and deep ties to every major chipmaker, and a startup promising to replace their tools has to prove its agents are reliable enough to trust with silicon that costs millions to fabricate.

That trust is the real product. For all the talk of speed, what ChipAgents has to sell is the confidence that an agent’s verification can be believed, and $60 million more is the market’s wager that it can get there.

The broader bet, shared across a field of AI-agent startups, is that agents will soon do skilled technical work, not merely talk about it.

content_html_zh:
ChipAgents 是一家构建设计和测试半导体的人工智能代理的初创公司，已筹集 6000 万美元。 该公司是英伟达的合作伙伴，它押注同样的代理人工智能重塑软件可以用于艰苦的芯片制造业务。

此次加薪让本已忙碌的一年雪上加霜。 ChipAgents 去年 10 月完成了 2100 万美元的 A 轮融资，并于 2 月份完成了 5000 万美元的一轮融资，因此最新的融资在不到一年的时间内使其总资金达到约 1.34 亿美元，这一速度与更广泛的人工智能原生芯片设计工具的热潮相匹配。

ChipAgents 首席执行官兼创始人 William Wang 表示：“我们正在帮助行业从人工智能助手转向能够执行有意义的工程工作的自主代理。”

该公司的产品位于被称为 EDA 的行业角落。 电子设计自动化是软件工程师用来布局和验证芯片的软件，这个市场长期由少数现有企业主导，而 ChipAgents 希望围绕自主代理而不是人类驱动的工具进行重建。

欧盟科技的💜

来自欧盟科技界的最新传言、我们明智的创始人鲍里斯的故事，以及一些值得怀疑的人工智能艺术。 每周都会免费发送到您的收件箱中。 立即注册！

验证是它所针对的瓶颈。 检查芯片是否真正完成其应有的功能会占用设计项目 70% 以上的时间，ChipAgents 表示，其代理可以读取规范、编写测试、运行测试并进行迭代，而无需工程师在每一步中进行操作。

这些主张是大胆的，正如它们通常的那样。 该公司表示，其代理商理解规范的速度比人类快很多倍，并且几乎立即生成正式检查，并且该平台已经在多家芯片制造商生产，尽管这些数据来自该公司而不是任何独立审计。

它的创始人将其视为模式的改变。 ChipAgents 首席执行官 William Wang 描述了代理“阅读规范、分解目标、讨论和实施解决方案、验证结果并不断迭代”，这是对完成工作而不是协助工作人员的软件的宣传。

该公司是 Alpha Design AI 的产品，总部位于圣何塞，其研究基地靠近圣巴巴拉。 王先生是一位学者出身的创始人，他依靠这一血统来招募人才和早期客户。

投资者基础一直以战略为主。 早期几轮融资吸引了 Bessemer Venture Partners 以及美光、联发科和爱立信等芯片界知名公司的参与，这些支持者的兴趣加倍表明该技术在行业内受到认真对待。

Nvidia的标签是最引人注目的部分。 路透社将 ChipAgents 视为 Nvidia 的合作伙伴，在 Nvidia 的芯片和软件处于人工智能热潮中心的市场中，这是一个有用的协会，尽管具体的合作条款并未明确说明。

这种想法并不孤单。 一波初创公司正在将人工智能推广到硅堆栈的不同层，从 Oxmiq 的芯片架构到 Kandou 的互连，而代理设计工具是这场竞争的最新前沿。

逻辑几乎是递归的。 人工智能需要更多的芯片，而芯片的设计速度慢且成本高，因此业界正在寻求人工智能来设计运行更多人工智能的芯片，这是投资者难以抗拒的循环。

现任者并没有停滞不前，这就是风险。 老牌的 EDA 供应商拥有自己的人工智能功能，并且与每家主要芯片制造商都有着深厚的联系，而一家承诺更换其工具的初创公司必须证明其代理足够可靠，足以信任花费数百万美元制造的芯片。

这种信任才是真正的产品。 对于所有关于速度的讨论，ChipAgents 必须推销的是对代理验证可信的信心，而市场对其能够实现这一目标的赌注是 6000 万美元。

人工智能代理初创公司普遍认为，更广泛的赌注是，代理将很快从事熟练的技术工作，而不仅仅是谈论它。
